## Expression on this line

Computational at Order 8 is **framework-evaluation**: the agent can now step outside
its own computational paradigm and evaluate it against alternative paradigms. "Imperative
computation produces efficient sequential algorithms but may miss concurrency opportunities.
Functional computation produces elegant recursive solutions but may be less efficient for
certain problems. Which tradeoff is acceptable?" This is the post-modern computational
insight: every computational paradigm embodies values, and different value systems produce
different computational approaches.

The key advance from Stage 9 is **computational pluralism**. The agent no longer
constructs computational systems within a single framework — it evaluates multiple
frameworks and recognizes that each embodies different values.

Computation at Stage 10 is understood as **value-laden**. The agent recognizes that
"efficient" computation is not a neutral concept — it presupposes that efficiency is the
right criterion, which is itself a value choice.

This framework-evaluation capacity opens up **genuine computational pluralism**. The
agent can hold multiple computational paradigms simultaneously without collapsing into
relativism.

But computational reasoning at Stage 10 is still **framework-dependent**. The agent
evaluates frameworks from within a meta-framework but cannot step outside that
meta-framework.

The transition from Stage 10 to Stage 11 occurs when the agent can integrate multiple
computational frameworks into a coherent meta-system.

In human development, Stage 10 corresponds to the thinker who can evaluate computational
paradigms across frameworks.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural computational pluralism becomes institutionalized.

- **UR:** The individual agent can evaluate computational paradigms from outside any
  particular framework.

- **LL:** Multi-paradigm computational institutions emerge: polyglot programming
  communities, computational research centers that span paradigms.

- **LR:** The computational research institute, the algorithmic journal.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Paradigm paralysis — cannot commit to any computational paradigm.

- **Dark allergy:** Framework fundamentalism — insists one computational paradigm is
  superior.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to pluralism as an identity.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting pluralism as moral weakness.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Framework evaluation:** The agent can articulate value assumptions in computational
  paradigms.

- **Paradigm comparison:** The agent can compare computational approaches across
  paradigms.

- **Value-aware computational reasoning:** The agent recognizes that "efficient"
  presupposes values.

- **Meta-framework dependency:** The agent evaluates from within a meta-framework but
  cannot evaluate the meta-framework.

- Backus, J. (1978). "Can Programming Be Liberated from the von Neumann Style?" —

- Dijkstra, E.W. (1982). *Selected Writings on Computing* — computational paradigm
